Welcome to Our School
A very warm welcome from Emma Reach, Interim Head of Salisbury Cathedral School, Wiltshire...
We are delighted you have taken a moment to visit our website and begin to build a picture in your mind of our fabulous school. We hope that, as you absorb the information and sense the atmosphere of our environment, it inspires you to get in touch with us and start a conversation about your hopes for your child.
There is something really unique about Salisbury Cathedral School and so many people remark on its special atmosphere. We are frequently visited by alumni who tell us they feel so lucky to have spent their formative years at SCS and that it was the nurturing care of our dedicated staff, the passion of our talented specialists in all disciplines and the security of our family community that they feel set them bounding forward into their future lives with confidence, aspiration and excitement.
When asked what the children felt were the greatest strengths of the school, they told us of many things they loved: the food, the grounds, the plays and trips out each term, but they all, without exception, told us of the incredible teaching and the fabulous sense of community that sit at the heart of the school.
Core Values
In Pre-Prep...
In the Pre-Prep we follow 4 core values which sit at the heart of daily school life and form the basis of every child’s pastoral and academic development.
In Prep...
We want to develop ourselves as well-rounded individuals and as responsible members of society. We focus on 8 core values at Salisbury Cathedral School which are explored in different ways during our time here. These are qualities we hope will continue to be important throughout our lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Salisbury Cathedral School - Prep Core Values
pageCache.text:
Prep Core Values
We want to develop ourselves as well-rounded individuals and as responsible members of society. We focus on 8 core values at Salisbury Cathedral School which are explored in different ways during our time here.
These are qualities we hope will continue to be important throughout our lives
Community
Community
We understand the needs of the world and work hard to ensure that those around us are happy.
Creativity
We celebrate creativity in all its forms and enjoy exploring our own and others’ creative ideas.
Discovery
Discovery
We ask questions and want to know answers. We see learning as something special that we want to keep in our lives.
Leadership
Leadership
We take our responsibilities seriously and understand that we are role models to others. We lead by example by communicating well in the expectation that others will follow.
Resilience
Resilience
We understand that sometimes we face challenges and we aim to approach these with a positive outlook and a desire to do well. We understand it is important to bounce back from failures.
Self-discipline
Self-discipline
We reflect on our own lives, taking responsibility for and managing our own choices, knowing when to ask for support and when to work independently in order that we may achieve our goals.
Teamwork
Teamwork
We recognise the different strengths in others and ourselves and we enjoy playing our role as part of a team.
Thinking
Thinking
We give consideration to our thoughts before sharing them, we self-reflect and embrace creative solutions to solving problems.

Aims, Mission and Values
This is the place where you can pinpoint the abiding Values of our school.
Running like a bright ribbon through every aspect of daily life here, they bring together our whole approach to the education, personal development and well-being of each child.
They are also the mechanism by which we deliver our Mission: ‘To develop the whole child, preparing them to make a positive influence in the world .’
We are passionate about the application and working practice of these Values, and so it is important to us that, as you wander through this website, you can actively trace their influence and capacity to lift everybody up, to be the best they can be. It is what makes all the difference.

1. By fostering and developing our dedication to a shared purpose with our core partners (parents, alumni, Salisbury Cathedral and CSA).
2. Through charitable activities and events with the wider community.

Head's Welcome
Welcome
A very warm welcome from Emma Reach, Interim Head of Salisbury Cathedral School, Wiltshire...
We are delighted you have taken a moment to visit our website and begin to build a picture in your mind of our fabulous school. We hope that, as you absorb the information and sense the atmosphere of our environment, it inspires you to get in touch with us and start a conversation about your hopes for your child.
There is something really unique about Salisbury Cathedral School and so many people remark on its special atmosphere. We are frequently visited by alumni who tell us they feel so lucky to have spent their formative years at SCS and that it was the nurturing care of our dedicated staff, the passion of our talented specialists in all disciplines and the security of our family community that they feel set them bounding forward into their future lives with confidence, aspiration and excitement.
When asked what the children felt were the greatest strengths of the school, they told us of many things they loved: the food, the grounds, the plays and trips out each term, but they all, without exception, told us of the incredible teaching and the fabulous sense of community that sit at the heart of the school.
One child said: ‘Everyone is kind here, and we look out for each other. Whenever we have an argument, we’ve always been able to sort it out by the end of the day with the help of our teachers.’ Another child told us they had just been awarded an academic scholarship and it that was their teachers who had believed in them, shown them they had strengths they hadn’t realised and helped them achieve something they hadn’t considered possible before. We are so heartened by the strength of these connections between everyone in the community and we can feel, palpably, the school’s motto at work in the everyday activities of education here. ‘Your child at our heart’ sings loudly through Salisbury Cathedral School and this resonates so deeply with our beliefs about education.
We are extraordinarily fortunate to live and work in the most beautiful of environments and the wonder of our setting is something we appreciate every day. Nestled under the sheltering presence of the cathedral itself, our children can roam in the tranquil grounds, able to play creatively, to feed their curiosity, extend their thinking and hone their sporting strengths through the use of specialist classrooms, our all-weather astro, swimming pool and extensive playing fields, including a superb Forest School space.
Nevertheless, education is about so much more than facilities. Developing children’s confidence and self-belief sit right at the heart of our educational philosophy. It is our absolute passion to create the best possible educational experience for young people, and, of course, both the culture and the practicalities of school life need to be right in order to realise this for all the children who come to Salisbury Cathedral School.
Every pupil here achieves academic success and we work in small classes with a strong tutoring system so that children have the benefit of an individual, tailored approach. Children at Salisbury Cathedral School are helped to develop their outgoing spirits through the warmth of the relationships they build with their teachers; and through enthusiastic, nurturing encouragement to make the most of new opportunities, to grow in independence, determination and resilience – all key skills for their lives both now and in the future.
The opportunities for young people at Salisbury Cathedral School are truly life-changing. Whether it is the journey towards becoming a chorister, representing the school in one of the many sports on offer, working hard to gain a scholarship to senior school, taking a cameo role in one of the fabulous dramatic productions or stepping up to become a member of one of our pupil committees, pushing at half-opened doors of opportunity and exploring what’s beyond is something we encourage all our pupils to do. This is how we help them build their identities, their characters, their individual talents and their aspiration for life.
We believe educating young people is the best job in the world and Salisbury Cathedral School is filled with dedicated and highly skilled practitioners who feel the same as us.
We very much hope you’ll come for a visit; we should love to welcome you and discuss how we can do the very best for your child and their future. Please click below to watch our school film.

pageCache.pageTitle: Salisbury Cathedral School - A word from  ...
pageCache.text:
A word from ...
A warm welcome
I often wonder if St Osmund, first Bishop of Salisbury, ever imagined his school would be thriving nearly a thousand years later? I certainly dream of SCS flourishing into the next century, and beyond.
It is my belief that institutions cannot stand still. If you are not moving forward, then you are falling behind.
That’s why we have ambitious plans to future proof our small school.
After all, as custodians of one of the oldest educational institutions in the world, we have a duty of care not only to our current pupils, but also to those who will follow in their footsteps.
Visitors, alumni, and their families often comment on the beauty of our site and its historic buildings. Every day, our school community enjoys the very view of Salisbury Cathedral immortalised by John Constable in 1823. Yet, as with every story, privilege comes with responsibility: our remarkable location brings unique challenges for planning and development. Our plans carefully balance the constraints of our historic site with the needs of a modern preparatory school.
Our biggest challenge is funding these ambitions. Without a large endowment or state or church funding, we rely on all forms of support from our wider school community — alumni, parents, friends, staff, and governors.
There are many ways to contribute, you can even Make A Donation right now. We are registered for Gift Aid, and we also encourage you to consider supporting SCS by leaving a bequest in your will, for more information visit the Legacy page.

Music Matters
Title
Music Matters
With your support, Music Matters will bring the joy of music into classrooms across Salisbury and give children the chance to benefit from Salisbury Cathedral School’s award-winning education.
The project aspires to:
The investment required to achieve these important goals is £70,000, meaning it will take a true community effort to succeed, and every donation will count. A donation of just £16 with Gift Aid (£20 without Gift Aid) will pay for an academic field trip for a child on a bursary. For double that amount, £32 with Gift Aid (£40 without Gift Aid) will fund a music lesson for an entire class at one of our partner schools. Follow the donation link below to discover more ways your generosity can make a difference.
Music Matters is inspired by John Powell MBE (1931–2024). John found his voice as a chorister in the Salisbury Cathedral Choir between 1941 and 1945. He always said that his time at school and in the choir “changed his life.” He went on to devote his life to music and philanthropy, greatly enhancing the musical life of our city and raising hundreds of thousands of pounds for charity.
“My father was passionate about supporting the community, raising funds, and inspiring young musicians, so it is an honour for the Music Matters fund to be dedicated to his memory.” Gillian Broadway, John’s daughter

Wrap Around Care
Wrap around care
Before school care
Pre-Prep pupils who arrive between 8.00am and 8.30am should go straight to Little Spires in the Blee Room where they will be looked after until 8.30am and taken to pre-prep.
Children may be dropped off from 7.30am for breakfast club in the Blee Room, although this can only be done by prior arrangement and will incur a charge.
Classrooms are open from 8.30am.
After school care
Pre-prep children finishing school at 3.30pm can be booked into Little Spires by prior arrangement. This finishes at 6.00pm by which time all children should be collected. Charges will be incurred for after school care, please refer to the fees section of the website.

Music
Music
“I believe we make extraordinary music at this school because it is laced with the happiness of our children.”
Music at Salisbury Cathedral School has gained a reputation for outstanding levels of accomplishment and performance and we are all very proud of that.
What is more important to us though, is how our music and singing has the power to enrich lives, and how it reaches out to every child embracing the talent they have to give at the point they are ready to and want to give it.
Music has well-documented benefits of helping children to develop a sense of teamwork practising and performing together, of developing a freedom of expression and creativity and of cultivating self-discipline. I believe there is something more it provides too, which cannot be underestimated. That is the enormous privilege of the one-to-one relationship between child and teacher that can emerge in instrumental and choral lessons. It is yet another strata of time and care that encourages children to not only progress their skills, but also to interact and communicate with a grown up about anything they may have on the minds. Of course, music itself has great powers of mindfulness and we are determined that every child here has the chance of benefitting from that.
Susie Lamb, Head of Music

Allowing children to discover their own interests for themselves and to develop these pursuits through broad and varied opportunities, we hope will set them on their own journey of discovery and achievement.

pageCache.text:
A word from...
A word from Mrs Bedford
A warm welcome to the boarding house from Jack and Katie Stredwick, House Parents
I watch the children spill across the lawn and in through our boarding house doors after their supper, noisy and jostling about. They are happy. They feel like they have come home.
When parents ask us about boarding life here, we tell them firstly and quite simply that we are a big family.
What that means is that our total focus is on bringing all the comforts of a warm and happy home life to the boarders, so they can get the very best out of their school days. It also means that within this loving family atmosphere, children are given the confidence to grow up, make lasting friendships and develop their personalities. In such a close-knit group there is always somebody to talk to and share feelings with, which is so important for children today. The boarding house team, including the matrons and house parents are forever vigilant, but moreover we make sure that all the children know that we have time for them, that there is space for them to express themselves and that their well-being is all that matters to us.
What we love telling parents about also is that there is an enormous amount of fun to be had amongst our happy band. Weekend trips such as trekking, swimming, bowling and zip wire activities are planned for the children to not only let off steam, but to feed their sense of discovery and help them explore their leadership and teamwork capabilities. Baking and the creative arts are always a fixture along with time to just relax together, play games and enjoy the deep sense of belonging that envelops every pupil here.
We are in our element when there is a birthday cake to organise, or fancy dress outfits to make for a party, or an outing to be arranged. This is all amidst the busy purpose of helping boarders with their kit and equipment whilst at the same time encouraging them with firm but guiding hands to take responsibility for themselves – because that is just what it would be like in a happy family.
Jack and Katie Stredwick, House Parents

A word from...
A word from Mrs Cunningham-Brown, Head of Pre-Prep
A warm welcome to Nursery and Pre-Prep from Linda Cunningham Brown
“Learning in the Pre-Prep is built around a freedom of expression and creativity from our children, which is nurtured and harnessed to help them progress in the most natural way.”
Embracing the magic of creativity, the diversity of dinosaurs and the properties of the lavender plant, and then weaving those interests, amongst so many others from the children, into our literacy and numeracy programme tells us things are rocketing along in the Pre-Prep. I am particularly fond of talking about this to visiting parents in order to bring alive the special atmosphere and the ethos of our Pre-Prep. Because when the children come to school brimming with their own ideas we can respond to their energy by giving them the time and space to explore and develop. That means everything to them and to us.
Our broad, multi-sensory approach has children flying through the doors in the morning eager for their day to begin, and even in the earliest years they quickly come to understand that what we offer is all for them as individuals. Alert children who display a quiet confidence, a cooperative kindness when working with others, and the courage to give their best when faced with a challenge, know they will always be recognised and encouraged at Salisbury Cathedral School. Indeed, it is these very qualities that we seek to encourage every day in our happy children, and are what we are most proud of. These are the values I find myself speaking about all the time to parents who naturally want to ensure the best possible start for their children.
Our busy programme of French, music, ICT, PE and ballet lessons with dedicated teachers brings another skills dimension to the children, as do the sprawling and beautiful outdoor spaces that they love playing and learning in. All of this combines in the most dynamic way to support our mantra in the Prep-Prep which is to lift the learning off the page and out of the classroom. In this way we can inspire all of our children to reach beyond themselves and come to know what they have to offer, to believe in themselves, and to be happy.
Linda Cunningham Brown, Head of Pre-Prep

pageCache.pageTitle: Salisbury Cathedral School - Apple Tree Nursery
pageCache.text:
Apple Tree Nursery
Nursery - new
Our Beautiful Apple Tree Nursery in the Heart of the Close
Welcome to our nurturing 'Apple Tree' Nursery, happy home to our Early Years children. This is where magic happens before our eyes every day! There is nothing more exciting than seeing our youngest children gaze with awe and wonder at life and its mystery unfolding before them, and we revel in providing the very best opportunities to nurture their curiosity, enthusiasm and love for learning. Our nursery children have the best of both worlds: a bespoke early years setting led by highly qualified practitioners nestled within the warmth and excitement of a wider school community where wider specialist opportunities are on offer. Combine this with woodland walks, forest activities and extensive outdoor play featuring as a natural part of their everyday experiences, our nursery children sparkle with joy each day and develop confidence with every step they take.
All Year-Round Provision
We recognise that every family has different needs, which is why our Nursery, welcoming children from the age of two, offers flexible care for up to 50 weeks of the year. Families can choose from three options: All Year Round (50 weeks), Term Time Only (following Salisbury Cathedral School term dates) or Term Time Plus (following Wiltshire school term dates), providing flexibility to suit different family routines and commitments.
Nursery Admissions
Salisbury Cathedral School Nursery welcomes children from age 2 and provides a joyful introduction to school life. Children can attend full-time or for a preferred number of sessions, ensuring a balance that meets the individual’s needs and provides both nurture and stimulation in their learning journey.
The recommended number of sessions for all our children is usually a minimum of three days. Fewer sessions may be considered for 2-year olds at the discretion of our Head of Nursery. We really do recommend that pupils increase to five mornings as a minimum in the term before moving to Reception.
We work with your child on an individual basis to support them as they settle into the Nursery. Typically, a parent and child will attend together for an hour in the first instance. Subsequent visits aim to help children feel comfortable and confident in their new environment, but the timings and duration of these will be agreed upon between you and the Head of Nursery.
To find out more about Nursery fees click here
Nursery Life
Our pupils take their first steps into the joys of nursery life when they join the Pippins class at just over 2 years old moving into the Russets class as they turn 3 years old. In Pippins, they are immersed in child-initiated play, where they can choose from a whole range of activities to spark their curiosity, and suit their needs and desires throughout the day. Their play and learning takes place in a beautifully equipped set of large, light classrooms, all enjoying free-flow into the outside learning area and enclosed garden. In addition, the children enjoy exploring the wider outdoor environment, with woodland walks, forest activities and exciting outdoor play featuring in their everyday experiences.
Being part of a wider school community brings many additional benefits. From the age of three, our Nursery children enjoy weekly specialist teaching in French, Music, Sport and Outdoor Learning, delivered by our experienced Prep School teachers, as well as Ballet with Miss Chloe from Salisbury Dance Studios. These wonderful opportunities introduce our youngest children to new experiences, helping them discover their interests, develop new skills and grow in confidence.
With access to our extensive school grounds and facilities, the support of their dedicated teachers and close connections with older pupils, our Nursery children benefit from a rich and varied learning environment in which they can flourish.
Whether you choose for your child to join us at age 2, 3 or 4, individualised learning is right at the heart of all we do at SCS. Our passion is to develop the whole child and, at the root of this has to sit happiness. Our little people need to feel safe, nurtured and loved, every moment of the day. Our staff have the highest qualifications and we provide generous ratios to ensure your child has warm and nurturing care throughout their time with us. In Pippins, where the legal ratio is 1:5, we choose to work to an enhanced ratio of 1:4, allowing even greater individual attention and support. In Bramleys and Russets, we maintain a ratio of 1:8, ensuring every child continues to benefit from high-quality care and meaningful interactions with our experienced team. In this way, they are able to build meaningful relationships with all the adults in the Nursery and are able to develop their skills through rich and immersive activities in all seven areas of the Early Years Framework.
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum and cover seven areas of learning and development through immersive, inter-disciplinary themes that encourage the children across the early years age range to explore, investigate, play creatively and above all, have fun!
The three prime areas are:
Personal, social and emotional development
Communication and language
Physical development
There are four further specific areas of learning and development:
We chart each child’s progress against these seven areas carefully to ensure we are providing tailor-made opportunities for them to develop at the right pace, with just the right amount of challenge. Children develop at such different rates in their early years that we need to make sure we get the balance right: we don’t want our little ones to be bored, but we also don’t want them to be overwhelmed so we work hard to create the right experience for each individual. As well as thematic learning activities, children are given exposure to phonics and numbers so that when they are ready, they are able to develop some of the core building blocks for their future curriculum.
There are so many benefits to joining a nursery within a school setting: it’s like a big family and we celebrate everyone in it! Our facilities are excellent and as well as their gorgeous tailor-made home, the children enjoy making use of the whole school site, whether it be the dining room for delicious home-cooked meals, the library for story time or an adventurous walk in the woods and gardens in search of the Gruffalo! The children come to know and feel secure with all the staff in our community so they feel comfortable with increasing numbers of people; they join the Pre-Prep for assembly; they take part in events to show their families what they’ve been up to; they develop lovely relationships with older ‘buddies’ in the school who enjoy playing games with them at break times or reading stories to them at ‘quiet time’, and, when the time for Reception comes, our nursery children are ready to make the exciting leap into in the ‘big school’ environment, knowing we’re right with them, every step of the way.
Every day is an open day at Apple Tree Nursery so please come and see us!

Art and DT
Art
Art
Pupils have the opportunity to explore a wide range of different skills and media including, ceramics, fabric design, printing, sewing, sketching, collage, wire modelling and 3D design. The art department follows a theme for each term allowing the pupils to generate a wealth of creative and excellent art which is displayed throughout the school.
Design Technology
In Design Technology children have the chance to develop the skills of construction using a wide range of materials, both through independent learning and collaborative work. More importantly though, this subject offers children the opportunities to be creative, to problem-solve and to think and plan laterally.
